paragraphs: Rabbi Yose ben Zimra the Kohen. Hyman says that Zimra’s granddaughter, the daughter of Rabbi Yose ben Zimra, married the son of our holy Rabbi, citing Yoma 78a and Ketubot 62b.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The entry’s headword is Zimra; “his son’s daughter” is therefore read as Zimra’s granddaughter, Rabbi Yose ben Zimra’s daughter. The William Davidson Ketubot 62b paragraph says Rabbi arranged his son’s marriage into Rabbi Yose ben Zimra’s house, without specifying the bride’s father in that paragraph; Yoma 78a identifies Rabbi Yose ben Zimra as a Kohen. Hyman’s more specific relationship is retained as his statement.

The whole selected Davidson Yoma 78a paragraph explicitly calls Rabbi Yose ben Zimra a Kohen. The whole selected Ketubot 62b paragraph describes arranging a son’s marriage into Rabbi Yose ben Zimra’s house, without naming the bride’s father in that paragraph. The headword-based reading of “his son’s daughter” as Zimra’s granddaughter is retained explicitly as Hyman’s account, not a newly established genealogy. The earlier mixed note stays verbatim; “our holy Rabbi” is not converted into a canonical identity binding.
